 SAN ANTONIO — More rain inbound to South Texas after a rainy Sunday. Patchy light to moderate rain will continue on and off through most of Sunday evening. 
 Overnight, more widespread rain will develop to the south and move north into early Monday morning.
 More rain inbound to South Texas after a rainy Sunday. Patchy light to moderate rain will continue on and off through most of Sunday evening. (SBG San Antonio) 
 This will create a messy Monday morning commute with moderate to heavy rain moving through in waves.
 Rain coverage becomes more scattered for the afternoon, but the entire day will have an elevated rain chance.
 More rain inbound to South Texas after a rainy Sunday. Patchy light to moderate rain will continue on and off through most of Sunday evening. (SBG San Antonio) 
 This will create another cool day, with temperatures in the upper 50s and lower 60s.
 Tuesday, mainly cloudy skies will continue but the rain chance becomes more isolated at 30%. Temperatures will hold in the middle to upper 60s with the clouds.
 More rain inbound to South Texas after a rainy Sunday. Patchy light to moderate rain will continue on and off through most of Sunday evening. (SBG San Antonio) 
 The sun will return Veterans Day Wednesday with temperatures back in the 70s.
 *****
 As steady rain continues throughout much of South Central Texas Sunday into the early week, we want to see your photos and videos capturing the downpour.
 According to the National Weather Service, periods of light to moderate rain are expected to last through early Tuesday. Rainfall totals are expected to be in the 1 to 4 inch range with pockets of higher amounts up to 6 inches. 
 Threat for flooding across most areas remains low however minor river/creek levels could rise. Be sure to avoid closed low water crossings and keep up with the latest closures here . 
 Be sure to share your rain photos/videos via Chime In . You could see your content on-air and online!
 Get the latest weathercast and view our interactive radar here .
 FORECAST 
 Rest of Today 
 Periods of rain through the day. Breezy NE winds and cool. Upper 50s to low 60s. Not much of a flood risk for our area, greater flood risk down near Corpus Christi.
 FLOOD WATCH remains in effect for La Salle, McMullen and Goliad Counties through Monday morning.
 Monday 
 Widespread rain continues. Some heavy, especially in the morning hours. Cool & breezy. Low 60s.
 Tuesday 
 Mostly cloudy with isolated to scattered showers still in the area. Near 70.
 Veterans Day Wednesday 
 Partly to mostly cloudy, mid 70s.
 Rest of the week 
 Sun returns. Low to mid 70s. Cold front Thursday brings slightly cooler temps Friday into next weekend (lows in 40s), highs upper 60s to low 70s.
